Devon (Product): Heads up — FinGrid is seeing 401s on Dedicated after a recent runtime tweak. Support wants an expedited path (hotfix vs next minor).
Maya (Support): Repro and logs attached — seems related to header parsing after token rotation. Error snippet: "auth: missing client-id header -> 401". Link: https://redwood.internal/logs/fingrid/401s
Luca (Eng Lead): If it's just header parsing in the auth module, should be a small patch. Cherry-pickable. Need to confirm regression window and impact surface.
Raj (SRE): Canary first to their tenant is fine. Need a deploy window and rollback steps. Watchlist: auth-fail-rate, 5xx, tail latency.
Irene (Sales): Customer has committed capacity and is escalating. They want ETA and clear comms. If hotfix, provide ETA by EOD.
Sam (QA): I can run the QA pass — will need repro steps and a small dedicated replica. If patch is small, test matrix ~ 4 automated + 2 manual sanity checks.
Maya (Support): Repro (quick):
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \ \ 
     -H "X-Client-ID:" "" https://dedicated.redwood/fingrid/api/v1/predict
# returns 401 when X-Client-ID header is empty/missing, used to accept optional header before runtime change
```
Luca (Eng Lead): Plan proposal: create hotfix branch, cherry-pick fix into release branch, run QA, canary to FinGrid tenant for 30m, then roll out. Est: 1.5d eng + 0.5d QA + SRE ops.
Raj (SRE): Proposed windows: tonight 02:00 UTC or tomorrow 10:00 PST. Customer prefers daytime — suggests 10:00 PST.
Irene (Sales): Confirmed: FinGrid prefers 10:00 PST. They want an in-window notification and a follow-up once rolled out.
Devon (Product): Decision — proceed with hotfix. Action items: 1) Luca open PR and label `hotfix`, 2) Sam validate tests, 3) Raj schedule canary (10:00 PST), 4) Maya send customer comms by 09:20 PST. I'll track follow-ups and backlog ticket for long-term fix.
deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled by Raj — canary to tenant `fingrid-prod` at 2026-03-22T17:00:00Z. Command: `/deploy --branch hotfix/auth-header --canary-tenant=fingrid-prod`
Raj (SRE): I'll run the deploy and monitor these dashboards: auth-fail-rate, 5xx-rate, p95 latency, token-cache-hit. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/auth-hotfix
Sam (QA): If rollback needed use: 
```bash
/deploy --rollback --tag hotfix-auth-v1
```
Maya (Support): Customer notified and acknowledged. They'll be on the call during the canary. :thumbsup:
Devon (Product): Marking as P1-derived hotfix. Creating PROD-8421 to add telemetry and guardrails to prevent recurrence; larger refactor into next minor.
Irene (Sales): Sales will offer credits if >5m customer impact; I'll coordinate post-deploy.
Luca (Eng Lead): PR opened: https://git.redwood/infra/commit/abcd1234 — tagging @sam for QA.
Raj (SRE): Posting live status to #incidents during deploy and tagging @oncall. I'll also attach a short rollback procedure in the thread.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started by Raj at 2026-03-22T17:00:12Z.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy succeeded at 2026-03-22T17:12:37Z — auth-fail-rate back to baseline, no 5xx spike.
Devon (Product): Great. Close loop items: 1) postmortem + timeline, 2) backlog task PROD-8421 with acceptance criteria for telemetry, 3) customer follow-up note.
Maya (Support): Sending customer summary now. Will attach screenshots and metrics from canary.
Irene (Sales): Customer pleased with cadence and fast resolution. Keeping ticket open until PROD-8421 is scheduled.
Luca (Eng Lead): Adding small regression test to CI so header parsing is covered going forward.
Raj (SRE): Closing oncall task, will update runbook with the exact deploy flags used.
Devon (Product): Thanks everyone — I'll file the rollout notes and ensure the backlog item lands in next planning sprint. :eyes:
